reason: The passage explicitly depicts the Hebrew people under systemic oppression in Egypt. Multiple elements confirm this: (1) They are enslaved, forced to perform hard labor making bricks ('לִלְבֹּן הַלְּבֵנִים'); (2) Their workload is deliberately intensified by Pharaoh ('תִּכְבַּד הָעֲבֹדָה עַל־ הָאֲנָשִׁים'); (3) They are physically beaten by Pharaoh's overseers ('וַיֻּכּוּ שֹׁטְרֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל'); (4) Basic materials for their work are withheld ('לֹא תֹאסִפוּן לָתֵת תֶּבֶן'); (5) They live in fear of violence ('פֶּן־ יִפְגָּעֵנוּ בַּדֶּבֶר אוֹ בֶחָרֶב'); (6) Pharaoh repeatedly refuses their requests for freedom, continuously exerting control over them as a captive people. The Hebrew terms for their servitude ('עֲבָדֶיךָ' - your servants, 'סִבְלֹתֵיכֶם' - your burdens) reinforce their status as an oppressed people.
